pathway.title: LendingTree, Inc. — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: First, LendingTree has deleveraged materially. Total debt principal fell from USD 474.7 million at December 31, 2024 to USD 397.0 million at June 30, 2026, and Adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 153.6 million for the twelve months to June 30, 2026, so total debt to Adjusted EBITDA fell from 4.56x to 2.58x and net debt to Adjusted EBITDA from 3.54x to 1.86x [CP-1]. Management's statement of net leverage of 2.4x at year-end 2025 agrees with the 2.39x computed here [CP-1, CP-1A].

Second, the improvement depends on the EBITDA definition. Adjusted EBITDA excludes non-cash compensation, which was about 22.0% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA, and litigation settlements; on EBITDA built from net income, interest, tax, depreciation and amortization the same debt is 3.10x for the twelve months to June 30, 2026 and 4.46x for FY2025 [CP-1]. The credit agreement's own EBITDA definition is not supplied, so covenant leverage cannot be computed.

Third, liquidity is strong and the maturity profile is clear. Cash was USD 110.8 million, the USD 75.0 million revolver had no borrowings, and only USD 4.0 million of the term loan falls due within twelve months; the final maturity of both facilities is August 21, 2030 [CP-1, CP-1A]. The financial covenant is a first lien net leverage ratio of 5.00 to 1.00 that is tested only when revolver usage exceeds USD 20.0 million, so with the revolver undrawn the term loan lenders have no routine maintenance test; this is the issuer's own summary, not a reading of the agreement [CP-1, CP-1A].

Fourth, earnings are sensitive to a single segment and a single partner. Insurance was 63.7% of FY2025 revenue and 66.8% of Q2 2026 revenue; Progressive Casualty Insurance supplied 27% of FY2025 revenue, about 42.4% of Insurance revenue on the rounded percentage [CP-1A]. Variable marketing spend was 70.8% of H1 2026 revenue, and variable marketing margin fell to 29.2% of revenue in H1 2026 from 33.8% in FY2024 [CP-1].

Fifth, momentum has softened. Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of USD 35.2 million was 16.3% below Q1 2026 and below the USD 38 to 40 million guided in April, variable marketing margin was USD 87.3 million against a USD 93 to 97 million guide, and management cut its full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA outlook to USD 145 to 152 million from USD 152 to 162 million [CP-1, CP-1A]. These outlooks are management claims.

Sixth, cash generation is good and interest is largely floating. Free cash flow was USD 73.9 million over the twelve months to June 30, 2026, about 48.1% of Adjusted EBITDA, after cash interest of USD 34.7 million [CP-1]. The term loan bears interest at Term SOFR plus 4.50% or 4.25%; the sources disclose no hedge, so a 100 basis point rise would cost about USD 4.0 million a year, 5.4% of LTM free cash flow (calculation P2).

Seventh, ownership and capacity for creditor-adverse action are not testable. There is no sponsor, no dividend in over ten years and no repurchase in 2024, 2025 or the first half of 2026, which is supportive behaviour; the founder died in October 2025, his heirs collectively hold a substantial stake, and incremental debt capacity under the facility is the greater of USD 58.0 million and 50% of consolidated EBITDA plus an unlimited amount if first lien net leverage does not exceed 3.10 to 1.00 [CP-1A]. On issuer-defined Adjusted EBITDA the ratio-based part alone could allow roughly USD 190.0 million of additional first lien net debt, illustrative only because the agreement's EBITDA definition is not supplied (calculation P5).

runs.text: Strength, deleveraging and cash conversion (Documentary Fact). LendingTree cut total debt principal by USD 77.7 million (16.4%) between December 31, 2024 and June 30, 2026 while growing Adjusted EBITDA, and capital spending was 0.96% of LTM revenue, which leaves most operating cash flow available for debt service [CP-1]. The mechanism is a low-capital marketplace model whose costs are mostly variable advertising, so cash conversion is high when demand is stable.

Strength, liquidity and maturity profile (Documentary Fact). Cash of USD 110.8 million plus an undrawn USD 75.0 million revolver is USD 185.8 million, about 46.4 times the USD 4.0 million due within twelve months, and no maturity other than scheduled amortization falls before August 21, 2030 [CP-1]. This removes near-term refinancing risk and gives time for the earnings base to prove durable.

Strength, creditor-friendly behaviour so far (Analyst Interpretation). The company has paid no cash dividend in over ten years, repurchased no shares in 2024, 2025 or the first half of 2026 despite a USD 96.7 million authorization, repaid its convertible notes in cash at maturity, and has no identified sponsor [CP-1A]. Behaviour is documented, but legal capacity depends on the credit agreement, which is not supplied.

Strength, diversified segments and flexible cost base (Management Language, qualified). Management says it adjusts selling and marketing spend dynamically with partner demand; the three segments respond to different cycles, although Insurance was 49.5% of FY2025 segment profit and 56.3% in Q2 2026 [CP-1A] (10-Q Q2 2026 page:30 for management's statement). This is management's characterisation; the Q2 2026 results show the flex is partial, as variable marketing margin fell while revenue grew.

Weakness, earnings quality and definitions (Documentary Fact). Adjusted EBITDA is issuer-defined and drives every leverage and cover ratio; add-backs include non-cash compensation of USD 29.2 million in FY2025 [CP-1]. Treating LTM non-cash compensation as a cost raises total debt to EBITDA from 2.58x to 3.05x, so the deleveraging is real but flattered, and covenant EBITDA may differ from either measure.

Weakness, concentration (Documentary Fact). Insurance was 66.8% of Q2 2026 revenue and one carrier supplied 27% of FY2025 revenue, with two carriers at 22% and 11% in FY2024 [CP-1A]. Carriers set advertising budgets by their own underwriting results and can cut them quickly, so a budget cut reduces revenue at once while the speed of the cost response is not documented in the sources.

Weakness, margin pressure and a weaker Q2 (Documentary Fact). Variable marketing margin was 27.9% of revenue in Q2 2026 against 33.4% in Q2 2025, Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA was below guidance, and management expects advertising costs to stay elevated [CP-1, CP-1A]. If media costs keep rising faster than partner fees, cash flow weakens while the debt stays fixed at USD 397.0 million.

Weakness, floating-rate debt and thin hard-asset cover (Documentary Fact). The term loan is floating, no hedge is disclosed, and goodwill and intangibles are 45.7% of total assets with negative tangible equity of USD 96.3 million (calculation P6). Creditor protection therefore depends on enterprise value rather than hard assets, which is a mechanic and not a recovery conclusion.

Weakness, governance transition and untested protections (Insufficient Information). The founder died in October 2025, the CEO changed on October 13, 2025, and the heirs hold a substantial, unquantified stake; a single holder above 20% is not named [CP-1A]. The credit agreement, proxy statement and any change of control terms are not supplied, so restricted payment capacity, guarantor coverage and the effect of an ownership change on tax attributes are unknown.

runs.text: No acquisition, disposal, sponsor transaction or capital markets issue is described in any pinned document after the refinancing, so the transaction record is one financing event and a set of earlier changes; any transaction after July 30, 2026 is Not supplied. The refinancing is dated August 21, 2025, status closed. LendingTree entered into the 2025 Credit Agreement, a US$475.0 million first lien facility made up of a US$75.0 million revolving facility and a US$400.0 million term loan, both maturing August 21, 2030 (10-K page:144; 10-Q Q2 2026 page:18, page:39). The use of proceeds, as the filings state it, was to refinance the 2021 Credit Facility and the 2024 Term Loan, which collectively had US$402.8 million outstanding, with the US$400.0 million term loan and cash on hand at par plus accrued and unpaid interest, and for working capital and general corporate purposes (10-K page:97, page:144). The repayments were US$242.5 million of the 2021 term loan and US$160.3 million of the 2024 term loan; the 2021 revolver was terminated (10-K page:148). The company recognised a loss on extinguishment of US$7.9 million, incurred financing costs of US$8.6 million on the term loan of which about US$0.8 million was expensed, and paid US$3.9 million of original issue discount (10-K page:97, page:146). Earlier, the 0.50% Convertible Senior Notes due July 15, 2025, issued in July 2020 for US$575.0 million, were reduced by repurchases and the remaining US$95.3 million was repaid in cash at maturity on July 15, 2025, so no convertible debt, hedge or warrant remains and the warrants expired on February 11, 2026 (10-K page:142, page:144; 10-Q Q2 2026 page:14). The 2025 Term Loan is secured by substantially all assets including 100% of the equity in certain domestic subsidiaries and 65% of the voting equity of certain foreign subsidiaries, and guaranteed on a senior basis by material domestic subsidiaries; the revolver carries a US$30.0 million letter of credit sublimit; the financial covenant is a first lien net leverage ratio of 5.00 to 1.00 tested only when revolver usage exceeds US$20.0 million; and incremental capacity is the greater of US$58.0 million and 50% of consolidated EBITDA plus an unlimited amount subject to first lien net leverage of 3.10 to 1.00 (10-K page:145, page:146). Pricing is Term SOFR plus 4.50%, or 4.25% once a Moody's corporate family rating of B2 (stable) or better was achieved, which the 10-K says happened in January 2026; a 1.0% soft call premium applied during the first six months after closing (10-K page:145, page:146). The term loan balance was US$397.0 million at July 30, 2026 with no revolver borrowings and US$75.0 million available (10-Q Q2 2026 page:39, page:40). The liquidity effect, from CP-1, is cash of US$110.8 million and an undrawn US$75.0 million revolver at June 30, 2026, before any letters of credit, which are Not supplied. Sponsor and use-of-proceeds distributions: none documented; there is no sponsor and no distribution in the pinned sources. Which entity is the borrower, which subsidiaries guarantee and the exact covenant definitions are Not supplied because the credit agreement, exhibit 10.39 incorporated from a Form 8-K filed August 21, 2025, is not in the pack (10-K page:161).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: LendingTree is a US online marketplace that matches consumers with lenders, insurers and other providers and is paid fees by those providers, mostly when a consumer request is delivered. It is a public company with no sponsor or controlling owner identified in the supplied sources. The business has three reportable segments, Home, Consumer and Insurance, and its recent growth has come from Insurance, where earnings depend on carriers' advertising budgets and on the cost of the online media LendingTree buys to attract consumers. The creditor-relevant structure is simple: one first lien credit facility, secured on substantially all assets and guaranteed by material domestic subsidiaries, no dividend in over ten years, no share repurchases in 2024, 2025 or the first half of 2026, and no pending acquisition or ownership transaction in the supplied documents. The main uncertainties are the concentration in Insurance and in one carrier, the loss of the founder in October 2025 with his heirs holding a substantial stake, a weaker Q2 2026 against the company's own guidance, and the absence of the credit agreement. Everything after July 30, 2026 is Not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No acquisition, disposal, sponsor transaction or capital markets issue is described in any pinned document after the refinancing, so the transaction record is one financing event and a set of earlier changes; any transaction after July 30, 2026 is Not supplied. The refinancing is dated August 21, 2025, status closed. LendingTree entered into the 2025 Credit Agreement, a US$475.0 million first lien facility made up of a US$75.0 million revolving facility and a US$400.0 million term loan, both maturing August 21, 2030 (10-K page:144; 10-Q Q2 2026 page:18, page:39). The use of proceeds, as the filings state it, was to refinance the 2021 Credit Facility and the 2024 Term Loan, which collectively had US$402.8 million outstanding, with the US$400.0 million term loan and cash on hand at par plus accrued and unpaid interest, and for working capital and general corporate purposes (10-K page:97, page:144). The repayments were US$242.5 million of the 2021 term loan and US$160.3 million of the 2024 term loan; the 2021 revolver was terminated (10-K page:148). The company recognised a loss on extinguishment of US$7.9 million, incurred financing costs of US$8.6 million on the term loan of which about US$0.8 million was expensed, and paid US$3.9 million of original issue discount (10-K page:97, page:146). Earlier, the 0.50% Convertible Senior Notes due July 15, 2025, issued in July 2020 for US$575.0 million, were reduced by repurchases and the remaining US$95.3 million was repaid in cash at maturity on July 15, 2025, so no convertible debt, hedge or warrant remains and the warrants expired on February 11, 2026 (10-K page:142, page:144; 10-Q Q2 2026 page:14). The 2025 Term Loan is secured by substantially all assets including 100% of the equity in certain domestic subsidiaries and 65% of the voting equity of certain foreign subsidiaries, and guaranteed on a senior basis by material domestic subsidiaries; the revolver carries a US$30.0 million letter of credit sublimit; the financial covenant is a first lien net leverage ratio of 5.00 to 1.00 tested only when revolver usage exceeds US$20.0 million; and incremental capacity is the greater of US$58.0 million and 50% of consolidated EBITDA plus an unlimited amount subject to first lien net leverage of 3.10 to 1.00 (10-K page:145, page:146). Pricing is Term SOFR plus 4.50%, or 4.25% once a Moody's corporate family rating of B2 (stable) or better was achieved, which the 10-K says happened in January 2026; a 1.0% soft call premium applied during the first six months after closing (10-K page:145, page:146). The term loan balance was US$397.0 million at July 30, 2026 with no revolver borrowings and US$75.0 million available (10-Q Q2 2026 page:39, page:40). The liquidity effect, from CP-1, is cash of US$110.8 million and an undrawn US$75.0 million revolver at June 30, 2026, before any letters of credit, which are Not supplied. Sponsor and use-of-proceeds distributions: none documented; there is no sponsor and no distribution in the pinned sources. Which entity is the borrower, which subsidiaries guarantee and the exact covenant definitions are Not supplied because the credit agreement, exhibit 10.39 incorporated from a Form 8-K filed August 21, 2025, is not in the pack (10-K page:161).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: revenue is fees per delivered consumer request (10-K page:12) and Insurance was 66.8% of Q2 2026 revenue (CP-1). Risk mechanic: carriers set advertising budgets by underwriting results, and the 10-Q says carriers "are broadly experiencing strong automotive underwriting results" (10-Q Q2 2026 page:24), so Insurance revenue is cyclical in carrier profitability and in rate competition; contracts for Home lenders can be terminated for convenience (10-K page:12). Credit implication: debt service capacity rests on one segment's demand cycle with no contracted revenue, so leverage tolerance should assume Insurance can reverse faster than fixed costs. Counter-evidence: the three segments have different cycles, and Insurance segment profit grew 25% in Q2 2026 (10-Q Q2 2026 page:31). No logged conflict counters this.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: variable marketing expense was 70.8% of H1 2026 revenue (CP-1) and management expects advertising costs to stay elevated (10-Q Q2 2026 page:35). Risk mechanic: media cost rising faster than monetisation compresses variable marketing margin before fixed costs, and the Q2 2026 variable marketing margin was 87.3 against 99.5 in Q1 2026 (CP-1). Credit implication: margin resilience is the key monitoring item, since Adjusted EBITDA for the covenant and for CP-1 leverage rests on it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Concentration risk. Evidence: Progressive Casualty Insurance was 27% of FY2025 revenue (10-K page:12), which on the rounded percentage is about 42.4% of Insurance revenue (calculation C3). Risk mechanic: a carrier can cut its budget at short notice, and QuoteWizard's own risk factors list "concentration of customers with large insurance carriers" (10-K page:27). Credit implication: a single relationship change could move Adjusted EBITDA materially; the contract terms and the 2026 share are Not supplied, so the exposure cannot be sized for 2026. Counter-evidence: in FY2024 two partners together supplied 33%, so concentration has shifted between names, not fallen.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: LendingTree is a moderate credit that is improving, with leverage now low for a high yield issuer but earnings that are volatile and concentrated. The strongest support is the balance sheet: USD 110.8 million of cash, an undrawn USD 75.0 million revolver, one facility maturing August 21, 2030 and USD 73.9 million of free cash flow over the last twelve months. The weakest point is earnings quality and concentration: Adjusted EBITDA adds back non-cash compensation, Insurance is 66.8% of Q2 2026 revenue, one partner supplied 27% of FY2025 revenue, and management lowered its 2026 outlook. What decides the outcome is whether carrier advertising budgets and media costs hold; the credit agreement, which is not supplied, would show how much protection the covenants give.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First, LendingTree has deleveraged materially. Total debt principal fell from USD 474.7 million at December 31, 2024 to USD 397.0 million at June 30, 2026, and Adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 153.6 million for the twelve months to June 30, 2026, so total debt to Adjusted EBITDA fell from 4.56x to 2.58x and net debt to Adjusted EBITDA from 3.54x to 1.86x [CP-1]. Management's statement of net leverage of 2.4x at year-end 2025 agrees with the 2.39x computed here [CP-1, CP-1A].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Second, the improvement depends on the EBITDA definition. Adjusted EBITDA excludes non-cash compensation, which was about 22.0% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA, and litigation settlements; on EBITDA built from net income, interest, tax, depreciation and amortization the same debt is 3.10x for the twelve months to June 30, 2026 and 4.46x for FY2025 [CP-1]. The credit agreement's own EBITDA definition is not supplied, so covenant leverage cannot be computed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third, liquidity is strong and the maturity profile is clear. Cash was USD 110.8 million, the USD 75.0 million revolver had no borrowings, and only USD 4.0 million of the term loan falls due within twelve months; the final maturity of both facilities is August 21, 2030 [CP-1, CP-1A]. The financial covenant is a first lien net leverage ratio of 5.00 to 1.00 that is tested only when revolver usage exceeds USD 20.0 million, so with the revolver undrawn the term loan lenders have no routine maintenance test; this is the issuer's own summary, not a reading of the agreement [CP-1, CP-1A].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fourth, earnings are sensitive to a single segment and a single partner. Insurance was 63.7% of FY2025 revenue and 66.8% of Q2 2026 revenue; Progressive Casualty Insurance supplied 27% of FY2025 revenue, about 42.4% of Insurance revenue on the rounded percentage [CP-1A]. Variable marketing spend was 70.8% of H1 2026 revenue, and variable marketing margin fell to 29.2% of revenue in H1 2026 from 33.8% in FY2024 [CP-1].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fifth, momentum has softened. Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of USD 35.2 million was 16.3% below Q1 2026 and below the USD 38 to 40 million guided in April, variable marketing margin was USD 87.3 million against a USD 93 to 97 million guide, and management cut its full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA outlook to USD 145 to 152 million from USD 152 to 162 million [CP-1, CP-1A]. These outlooks are management claims.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sixth, cash generation is good and interest is largely floating. Free cash flow was USD 73.9 million over the twelve months to June 30, 2026, about 48.1% of Adjusted EBITDA, after cash interest of USD 34.7 million [CP-1]. The term loan bears interest at Term SOFR plus 4.50% or 4.25%; the sources disclose no hedge, so a 100 basis point rise would cost about USD 4.0 million a year, 5.4% of LTM free cash flow (calculation P2).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Seventh, ownership and capacity for creditor-adverse action are not testable. There is no sponsor, no dividend in over ten years and no repurchase in 2024, 2025 or the first half of 2026, which is supportive behaviour; the founder died in October 2025, his heirs collectively hold a substantial stake, and incremental debt capacity under the facility is the greater of USD 58.0 million and 50% of consolidated EBITDA plus an unlimited amount if first lien net leverage does not exceed 3.10 to 1.00 [CP-1A]. On issuer-defined Adjusted EBITDA the ratio-based part alone could allow roughly USD 190.0 million of additional first lien net debt, illustrative only because the agreement's EBITDA definition is not supplied (calculation P5).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Strength, deleveraging and cash conversion (Documentary Fact).** LendingTree cut total debt principal by USD 77.7 million (16.4%) between December 31, 2024 and June 30, 2026 while growing Adjusted EBITDA, and capital spending was 0.96% of LTM revenue, which leaves most operating cash flow available for debt service [CP-1]. The mechanism is a low-capital marketplace model whose costs are mostly variable advertising, so cash conversion is high when demand is stable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Strength, liquidity and maturity profile (Documentary Fact).** Cash of USD 110.8 million plus an undrawn USD 75.0 million revolver is USD 185.8 million, about 46.4 times the USD 4.0 million due within twelve months, and no maturity other than scheduled amortization falls before August 21, 2030 [CP-1]. This removes near-term refinancing risk and gives time for the earnings base to prove durable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Strength, creditor-friendly behaviour so far (Analyst Interpretation).** The company has paid no cash dividend in over ten years, repurchased no shares in 2024, 2025 or the first half of 2026 despite a USD 96.7 million authorization, repaid its convertible notes in cash at maturity, and has no identified sponsor [CP-1A]. Behaviour is documented, but legal capacity depends on the credit agreement, which is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Strength, diversified segments and flexible cost base (Management Language, qualified).** Management says it adjusts selling and marketing spend dynamically with partner demand; the three segments respond to different cycles, although Insurance was 49.5% of FY2025 segment profit and 56.3% in Q2 2026 [CP-1A] (10-Q Q2 2026 page:30 for management's statement). This is management's characterisation; the Q2 2026 results show the flex is partial, as variable marketing margin fell while revenue grew.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Weakness, earnings quality and definitions (Documentary Fact).** Adjusted EBITDA is issuer-defined and drives every leverage and cover ratio; add-backs include non-cash compensation of USD 29.2 million in FY2025 [CP-1]. Treating LTM non-cash compensation as a cost raises total debt to EBITDA from 2.58x to 3.05x, so the deleveraging is real but flattered, and covenant EBITDA may differ from either measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Weakness, concentration (Documentary Fact).** Insurance was 66.8% of Q2 2026 revenue and one carrier supplied 27% of FY2025 revenue, with two carriers at 22% and 11% in FY2024 [CP-1A]. Carriers set advertising budgets by their own underwriting results and can cut them quickly, so a budget cut reduces revenue at once while the speed of the cost response is not documented in the sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Weakness, margin pressure and a weaker Q2 (Documentary Fact).** Variable marketing margin was 27.9% of revenue in Q2 2026 against 33.4% in Q2 2025, Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA was below guidance, and management expects advertising costs to stay elevated [CP-1, CP-1A]. If media costs keep rising faster than partner fees, cash flow weakens while the debt stays fixed at USD 397.0 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Weakness, floating-rate debt and thin hard-asset cover (Documentary Fact).** The term loan is floating, no hedge is disclosed, and goodwill and intangibles are 45.7% of total assets with negative tangible equity of USD 96.3 million (calculation P6). Creditor protection therefore depends on enterprise value rather than hard assets, which is a mechanic and not a recovery conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Weakness, governance transition and untested protections (Insufficient Information).** The founder died in October 2025, the CEO changed on October 13, 2025, and the heirs hold a substantial, unquantified stake; a single holder above 20% is not named [CP-1A]. The credit agreement, proxy statement and any change of control terms are not supplied, so restricted payment capacity, guarantor coverage and the effect of an ownership change on tax attributes are unknown.
